notes: Lists updates as text using host configuration. Linux uses the existing APT cache (does not refresh it) or DNF, without mustra patch-list repository scoping. No post-install refresh hook.

commands.linux:
# Standalone example: Lists updates as text using host configuration. Linux uses the existing APT cache (does not refresh it) or DNF, without mustra patch-list repository scoping. No post-install refresh hook.
if command -v apt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  apt list --upgradable
else
  dnf check-update
  result=$?
  if [ "$result" -ne 0 ] && [ "$result" -ne 100 ]; then exit "$result"; fi
fi
commands.darwin:
# Standalone example: Lists updates as text using host configuration. Linux uses the existing APT cache (does not refresh it) or DNF, without mustra patch-list repository scoping. No post-install refresh hook.
softwareupdate -l
commands.windows:
# Standalone example: Lists updates as text using host configuration. Linux uses the existing APT cache (does not refresh it) or DNF, without mustra patch-list repository scoping. No post-install refresh hook.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$session = New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session
$searcher = $session.CreateUpdateSearcher()
$searcher.Search('IsInstalled=0 and IsHidden=0').Updates | ForEach-Object { $_.Title }
